start_hints.notes: lambda from method-of-moments via the second-moment ratio (alpha0 = 2(s - m^2)/(s - 2 m^2), lambda0 = 1/(m(alpha0 - 1))); kappa is closed-form given lambda.

implementation.algorithm: MOM init for lambda, 1D Newton on lambda, closed-form kappa = n/sum(log1p(lambda*x))

docs.title: Lomax distribution maximum likelihood estimation
docs.description: Estimates Lomax (Pareto Type II) parameters via Newton–Raphson on lambda, with kappa in closed form given lambda.
docs.details: The Lomax MLE only exists when the data show enough dispersion: specifically `mean(x^2) >= 2 * mean(x)^2` (equivalently, sample CV >= 1). Below that threshold the likelihood has no interior maximum: as `kappa -> Inf` with `lambda * kappa` held constant the Lomax density converges to an Exponential, and the likelihood approaches that limit without ever attaining it. `mllomax()` detects this at entry and stops with a message recommending `mlexp()`. Inputs that satisfy the moment condition are fit by Newton-Raphson on lambda; kappa is then `n / sum(log1p(lambda * x))`.
references: Kleiber, C. and Kotz, S. (2003) Statistical Size Distributions in Economics and Actuarial Sciences. Wiley.

Giles, D. E., Feng, H. and Godwin, R. T. (2013) On the bias of the maximum likelihood estimator for the two-parameter Lomax distribution. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 42(11), 1934-1950.
